ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The image is a Ksp table, with columns Name, Formula, Ksp. The table lists: Cadmium carbonate, CdCO3, Ksp = 5.2×10^-12; Cadmium hydroxide, Cd(OH)2, Ksp = 2.5×10^-14; Calcium fluoride, CaF2, Ksp = 3.9×10^-11; Silver iodide, AgI, Ksp = 8.3×10^-17; Zinc carbonate, ZnCO3, Ksp = 1.4×10^-11. Then reason: For 1:1 type salts CdCO3, AgI, ZnCO3, the solubility s satisfies Ksp = s^2, so s = sqrt(Ksp). CdCO3: s = sqrt(5.2×10^-12) ≈ 2.3×10^-6 M; AgI: s = sqrt(8.3×10^-17) ≈ 9×10^-9 M; ZnCO3: s = sqrt(1.4×10^-11) ≈ 3.7×10^-6 M. For Cd(OH)2 and CaF2, the dissolution equations are respectively Cd(OH)2 ⇌ Cd^2+ + 2OH^- and CaF2 ⇌ Ca^2+ + 2F^-, therefore Ksp = s(2s)^2 = 4s^3, s = (Ksp/4)^(1/3). Cd(OH)2: s = (2.5×10^-14/4)^(1/3) ≈ 1.8×10^-5 M; CaF2: s = (3.9×10^-11/4)^(1/3) ≈ 2.1×10^-4 M. Comparing these molar solubilities, the largest is CaF2.

method.method_draft: Group the compounds by dissolution stoichiometry using the formulas in the table.
